items.title: The Final Push - THE GRIND Episode 3 | A Monster Energy Documentary Series
items.description:
Nine rounds. Three riders. One season.

Every season has a beginning. Every race brings new challenges. But only one finish line marks the end.

In the final episode of THE GRIND, follow Luca Martin, Charlie Aldridge and Gwendalyn Gibson through the closing chapter of the 2026 UCI Cross-Country World Cup season, from Les Gets to the final round in Lake Placid, New York.

After a season full of pressure, setbacks and defining moments, everything comes down to the final races.

Luca Martin fights to secure the overall titles in both XCO and XCC. Charlie Aldridge, after a difficult start to the season, finds his way back to the top and finishes the year with a UCI World Cup victory. Gwendalyn Gibson reaches a new milestone in her career with an incredible second place at Soldier Hollow.

Three different journeys. Three different definitions of success. One final push.

More than a race recap, THE GRIND goes behind the results to explore the people, the sacrifices and the moments that define a season at the highest level of Cross-country mountain biking.

This is the end of the season. This is THE GRIND.

Presented by Monster Energy. 🟢

items.title: Anna Newkirk Thought She Was Going Slow - Then Won a World Cup
items.description:
Anna Newkirk is officially a Downhill World Cup winner. But the secret to her breakthrough wasn't riding harder - it was learning when to stop trying so hard.

Anna returns to the Downtime Podcast to take us inside her incredible first Elite World Cup victory at Lenzerheide, where she overcame nerves, self-doubt and a chaotic race morning to deliver the biggest result of her career.

We get into what it felt like dropping last, the surreal moment she realised she'd won, and why becoming the first American woman in 23 years to win an Elite Downhill World Cup wasn't quite the experience she'd imagined.

Anna also opens up about the difficult journey to that moment, from her breakthrough podiums with Frameworks Racing to a serious hand injury at Val di Sole, a frustrating recovery and the challenge of rebuilding her confidence.

We discuss how factory support has changed her racing, the physical and mental work behind her return to form, why different tracks demand completely different mindsets, and how she's learning to manage the expectations that come with knowing she can win.

There's also plenty of bike talk, including the latest Frameworks developments, suspension setup and her experience trying Neko Mulally's enormous 32-inch-wheel prototype.

Anna has proved she has the speed to win at the very highest level.

Now the challenge is finding the right recipe to do it more often.

items.title: Building the Perfect Bike for Red Bull Hardline British Columbia
items.description:
Practice is under way at Red Bull Hardline British Columbia, and the brand new track is already making an impression.

Rob pops round the pits to see how bikes are being tuned while Eliot heads on course to get the latest scoop. 

Nobody has raced on Cypress Hill before, so everyone is working it out at the same time.That’s also why so much is changing on the bikes this week. Suspension, tires, bar height and spoke tension. On a track this size, those decisions are the difference between a clean run and a frustrating one.

items.title: What Happens When You Ignore the Rules of Downhill Bike Design?
items.description:
One of the most unconventional bikes on the Downhill World Cup circuit is proving its worth.

After leaving a factory team to pursue his own vision of the ultimate downhill race bike, Reece Wilson teamed up with Gamux to challenge conventional bike design. With a Gates belt drive, gearbox drivetrain, radical geometry, and an unusual cockpit setup, almost nothing about this bike follows the traditional formula.

Made in partnership with Gates

items.title: After Years of Prototyping, We Finally Get to Ride It - Norco Team DH
items.description:
For the past five years, we’ve patiently waited for Norco to release the production version of its next downhill bike. We watched multiple versions raced at World Cups, including Gracey Hemstreet racking up three wins on the bike in 2025. And now that it's finally here, it offers plenty to talk about.

With plenty to dive into, we spent a few days testing the Team DH in the Whistler Bike Park to see what all these years of development have produced.
